exercises.q: А на ___ (четвёртый год, acc. sg.) уж и водоливом пошел, — показал хозяину разум свой!..
exercises.why: **год → год** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **четвёртый → четвертый** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with год). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. год · года · году · год · годом · годе; pl. годы · годов · годам · годы · годами · годах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Вообще на ___ (седьмой год, acc. sg.) своей жизни в монастыре Сергию стало скучно.
exercises.why: **год → год** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **седьмой → седьмой** (acc. sg. m., agreeing with год). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ый): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. год · года · году · год · годом · годе; pl. годы · годов · годам · годы · годами · годах.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Он ___ (весь вечер, acc. sg.) усиленно угощал меня текилой.
exercises.prompt: He plied me with tequila all evening.

Its forms (m. sg.): весь · всего · всему · весь (inan.) / всего (anim.) · всем · всём. exercises.q: Том ___ (вся неделя, acc. sg.) чихает.
exercises.prompt: Tom has been sneezing all week.
exercises.why: **неделя → неделю** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -я. Declines like DLI's неделя — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. неделю). Ending -я → -ю.  **весь → всю** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with неделю). «весь» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (f. sg.): вся · всей · всей · всю · всей · всей.  Declension: sg. неделя · недели · неделе · неделю · неделей · неделе; pl. недели · недель · неделям · недели · неделями · неделях.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Да я у них похудел в ___ (одни сутки, acc. pl.).
exercises.why: **сутки → сутки** (acc. pl.). A plural-only noun (it has no singular); nominative plural сутки. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **один → одни** (acc. pl., agreeing with сутки). «один» is a pronoun-type word with its own declension, not the regular adjective pattern, so no ending rule is claimed. Its forms (pl.): одни · одних · одним · одни (inan.) / одних (anim.) · одними · одних.  Declension (plural only): сутки · суток · суткам · сутки · сутками · сутках.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «The letter ы never follows г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ; therefore: книга — книги, река — реки, госпожа — госпожи.» — DLI, Lesson 23.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
